Given MCP is enabled with default configuration, when the listener starts, then it binds to 127.0.0.1 and rejects non-loopback remote addresses before MCP tool dispatch.
Given whitelist mode is requested without direct TLS or trusted TLS proxy transportSecurity, when the config is validated, then the config is rejected and the existing MCP listener remains unchanged.

Given trusted TLS proxy mode is enabled, when a request arrives, then forwarded client IP headers are trusted only if the immediate remote address is in trustedProxies and the forwarded protocol is HTTPS; otherwise the request is rejected before whitelist matching.

Given an MCP or webhook request has a remote address, effective client IP, Origin, or token that fails policy, then the response contains an observable error code and audit id without disclosing token, key, or raw prompt material.

Given the MCP port or bind host changes, when rebind succeeds, then a candidate listener is health-probed, swapped active, and the old listener is drained without restarting the app HTTPS server or redirect server.

Given MCP rebind fails during validation, candidate bind, health probe, or persistence, then the previous listener and persisted config remain active and the failure is visible through MCP control status and audit.

Given an MCP client calls tools/list, then the response includes buildergate.session.whoami, buildergate.session.claim, buildergate.session.list, buildergate.session.search, buildergate.message.send, buildergate.session.set_alias, buildergate.session.open_agent, buildergate.session.close, buildergate.session.close_self, buildergate.message.reply_to_leader, and buildergate.session.update_status with JSON input schemas.

Given a session-bound actor calls buildergate.session.whoami, then the result includes sessionId, sessionKey, workspaceId, tabId, alias, agentKind, leaderSessionKey, bindingLifecycle, and agentStatus.

Given a legacy or manually configured session lacks a session-bound token, when Streamable HTTP initialization presents a valid one-time claim code as its Bearer bootstrap credential and that transport session calls buildergate.session.claim with the same code, then the code must be unexpired, bound to an existing live session, atomically consumed once, and exchanged for a registered session-bound actor token. Claim codes expire after five minutes, their server-side collection is pruned and limited to 256 records, and reuse, expiration, or a non-live binding is rejected with a stable denial code. Every subsequent POST carrying mcp-session-id must also present the exact Bearer used at initialization; the claim bootstrap transport continues presenting its original claim code after binding while the server authorizes through the internally minted actor token. Missing, mismatched, or browser-JWT credentials are rejected, an unbound bootstrap session may discover or call only the claim flow plus protocol initialization and ping operations, and every session capability is revalidated against its current live binding on each request. Once an authorized close begins, all registered actor tokens for that session are revoked even if later tab or process cleanup reports failure.
Given a tool call fails validation or policy, then the MCP response maps the failure to a stable observable error code rather than silently falling back to a different tool or target.

Given the MCP implementation exchanges JSON-RPC messages over Streamable HTTP, then request and response bodies are UTF-8 JSON and tool names remain ASCII even when aliases such as 빌더 게이트 or 클로드 are used in arguments.

Given a runtime terminal session is created, when the MCP registry binds it, then sessionId is a UUID generated by SessionManager and sessionKey remains stable for the tab across restart and orphan recovery.

Given a tab restart or orphan recovery replaces WorkspaceTab.sessionId, when registry reconciliation runs, then currentSessionId and generation are updated while the previous sessionId becomes stale for MCP targeting.

Given a tool call targets a sessionId that does not match the current binding generation, then the call fails with STALE_SESSION_ID and returns enough non-secret binding context for the caller to re-search or retarget.

Given buildergate.session.list is called with includeSelf true or false, then it returns live bindings with sessionId, sessionKey, alias, nameSource, workspaceId, tabId, agentKind, agentStatus, mcpConnected, and leaderSessionKey according to the includeSelf option.
Given the user renames the lower status-bar session name or tab name, when WorkspaceTab.name is saved with nameSource user, then MCP list and exact alias search use that value as the primary alias.
Given buildergate.session.set_alias succeeds, then it updates the same WorkspaceTab.name and nameSource user path used by UI rename and broadcasts tab:updated to connected clients.

Given buildergate.session.search receives a query such as 빌더 게이트, then exact user alias match is ranked before terminal-title names, tab prefixes, agent aliases, cwd, or recovery-command matches; zero matches, ambiguous equal-rank matches, stopped bindings, and unauthorized targets fail with explicit candidate or reason data.

Given WebSocket user input, restore input, buildergate.message.send, buildergate.message.reply_to_leader, open_agent command injection, kickoff, or webhook delivery is submitted, when input is accepted, then the final PTY write occurs through SessionInputGateway rather than each caller directly invoking SessionManager.writeInput.

Given replay or screen-repair state is pending for a target session, when MCP or webhook input is submitted, then the gateway queues or rejects according to the configured replayPolicy and returns INPUT_REJECTED_REPLAY_PENDING or equivalent observable status when rejected.

Given a message uses paste-only delivery, then the gateway writes text without synthetic Enter submission and rejects carriage return, line feed, or submit semantics unless the actor has mcp:message.submit scope and the request explicitly sets submit true.
Given a hidden, closed, retired, stale-generation, or non-live target is selected, then the gateway rejects the delivery with a stable error code and does not call the PTY write path.

Given an AI TUI session receives user typing, local echo, prompt redraw, cursor movement, ticker output, or waiting-input repaint, then the shared input path preserves the existing invariant that those events do not transition the session to running.

Given a follower calls buildergate.message.reply_to_leader, then the gateway resolves the leaderSessionKey to a live binding and reuses message delivery; if the leader is unavailable, the follower remains open and the error is returned.

Given an admin creates or edits an agent profile, then command, args, aliases, isDefault, enabled, kickoffPrompt, and mcpClientConfigMode are stored in a dedicated agent profile store rather than in command presets or recovery options.

Given buildergate.session.open_agent is called, then the launch flow preallocates sessionKey, draft binding, launch attempt, and scoped capability token before creating the workspace tab and PTY session.

Given a profile uses env or generated-file MCP client config mode, when the PTY process is spawned, then MCP URL, sessionKey, current sessionId, leaderSessionKey, and capability token or generated config path are available at spawn time rather than attached after tab creation.

Given automatic config is not supported for a profile, when manual mode is used, then the response exposes a one-time claim code that is configured as the Streamable HTTP initialization Bearer credential, and the resulting claim-only transport session can bind by calling buildergate.session.claim with that same code before using session-bound tools.
Given an agent command is injected, then the injection uses SessionInputGateway with purpose agent-command and does not bypass the same enter, replay, and audit policy as other MCP input.

Given agent readiness is detected by buildergate.session.update_status or an approved foreground detector, then kickoffPrompt is delivered as a kickoff assignment through SessionInputGateway; if readiness times out, kickoff is not pasted automatically and the response reports kickoffPending true.

Given buildergate.session.update_status is called by a bound actor, then agentKind, agentStatus, detail, lastSeenAt, and MCP connected state update the live registry and are visible in list and search results.

Given open_agent fails before tab or PTY creation, then no workspace tab or runtime session is left behind, minted capability tokens are revoked, generated config files are deleted, and the launch attempt is recorded as cancelled or failed with an observable error code.

Given open_agent creates a tab or PTY and then binding finalization or command injection fails, then the compensation path calls WorkspaceService.deleteTab once, revokes tokens, deletes generated files, marks the launch attempt failed, and records cleanup success or failure.

Given agent command injection succeeds but readiness times out, then the session remains open, agentStatus remains unknown or starting, kickoffPending is true, and no automatic close or unsafe kickoff paste occurs.

Given buildergate.session.close is authorized for another session, then tab and PTY cleanup go through WorkspaceService.deleteTab and MCP code does not call SessionManager.terminateSession a second time for the same tab-close operation.
Given buildergate.session.close_self is called without leaderSessionKey, then it fails with SELF_CLOSE_DENIED_NO_LEADER and does not close the user-created session.

Given buildergate.session.close_self is called by a follower with a live leaderSessionKey, then the tool returns an accepted close job before scheduling tab and PTY cleanup 250 to 1000 milliseconds after response flush.
Given any close path completes or fails, then registry bindingLifecycle, tab removal broadcast, process-tree cleanup evidence, and audit result remain consistent and traceable.
Given a webhook key is created, then the UI receives the full random key only in the creation response, while storage persists keyId, keyHash, createdAt, expiresAt, and revokedAt without the raw key.
Given GET /webhook/agent is called with a query key and prompt, then prompt is accepted only when its UTF-8 query value is at most 2048 characters; larger prompts require POST body delivery.

Given a webhook request is invalid, revoked, expired, over rate limit, outside IP policy, or on an invalid transport, then the request is rejected with a stable error code and audit id before search, open_agent, or message delivery side effects occur.
Given a webhook request creates an assignment, then sourceSessionKey or caller session id is recorded exactly as the string "0" and the audit record marks actorType webhook.

Given a webhook request includes a target alias, then the system reuses buildergate.session.search resolution and message delivery semantics, including ambiguous target failure and paste-only default delivery.

Given a webhook request omits a target, then the system resolves the enabled default agent profile and uses open_agent; if no enabled default exists, the webhook fails without silently choosing another command.

Given webhook access logging, audit logging, and UI listing occur, then query strings, raw random keys, tokens, and raw long prompts are not persisted; only masked keys, key ids, prompt hash, and safe prompt preview are stored.
Given the Header Tools menu is opened, then it includes an MCP session control entry that opens a WindowDialog without navigating to the general Settings page.
Given the dialog is open, then it exposes tabs for sessions, agents, MCP, security, and webhooks with accessible tab and panel semantics consistent with existing tool dialogs.
Given an admin edits agent profiles, then the UI validates command, args, aliases, default, enabled, kickoffPrompt, and mcpClientConfigMode and saves them through mcpControlApi.

Given an admin edits MCP listener config, then the UI exposes enabled, host, port, bindMode, transportSecurity, trustedProxies, externalWhitelist, allowedOrigins, current listener status, last error, and rebind result; failed saves show an alert and keep the old endpoint active.

Given whitelist mode is selected, then the security tab requires direct TLS or trusted TLS proxy configuration and displays server validation errors for invalid CIDR, Origin, proxy, or transport settings.

Given a webhook key is created, rotated, revoked, or listed, then the UI shows the full key only in the creation response and otherwise displays masked key material, key id, last used status, and rate-limit status.
Given a live session alias is changed from the MCP dialog or by the lower status-bar rename, then the UI reflects the same WorkspaceTab.name and nameSource user value after tab:updated propagation.

Given the administrator selects fixed MCP access-key generation or regeneration in the security tab, then the dialog requires an explicit confirmation before the request, clears any previously displayed plaintext before opening confirmation, displays the newly generated key only after a successful response, and provides a Korean-labelled copy action beside that key. The copy action writes exactly the plaintext key without prefixes, whitespace, or metadata. Cancelling, failing, reloading, changing tabs, closing the dialog, or completing an in-flight response after any such dismissal must not restore a prior plaintext key.

Given any MCP tool call, webhook invocation, status update, alias change, input delivery, launch, close, or policy rejection occurs, then an audit event records actorType, actorSessionKey when present, source IP when available, tool or action, target binding when present, scope set, result, reason, request id or audit id, and redacted prompt hash or preview when applicable.
Given audit or access logs are written, then raw JWTs, MCP tokens, webhook random keys, full query strings, and raw long prompts are not persisted.

Given MCP listener status is requested by the UI, then enabled, bind host, port, listener status, active connection count, last rebind result, last error, and rejected request counters by reason are available.

Given live sessions are listed, then each binding exposes alias, agentKind, agentStatus, bindingLifecycle, mcpConnected, leader, workspace, tab, current sessionId, sessionKey, and lastSeenAt without exposing secret tokens.

Given an assignment is created from MCP or webhook delivery, then assignment status transitions from created to resolved to delivered or failed and remains queryable with prompt hash, prompt preview, deliveryMode, target, source, and audit id.

Given implementation is reported complete, then server unit tests, MCP Streamable HTTP integration tests, frontend unit tests, and Playwright core E2E on https://localhost:2222 cover loopback security, whitelist/proxy rejection, tool schemas, search and send, open_agent ready and kickoff gating, reply_to_leader, close_self, webhook key flow, redaction, and Tools dialog behavior.
Given a validation scenario cannot be executed, then the completion report records it as skipped or remaining operational validation instead of claiming coverage.

Given an MCP session token is minted, then it carries audience buildergate-mcp, scope, expiration, jti, and sessionKey when session-bound; the raw token is not persisted and replayed, expired, wrong-audience, or wrong-session tokens are rejected.

Given a default session-bound actor is created, then its default scopes are exactly mcp:self.read, mcp:sessions.list, mcp:message.paste, and mcp:status.write; mcp:message.submit, mcp:session.open, mcp:sessions.alias.write, mcp:session.close, and mcp:session.close_self require explicit additional grants.

Given a leader creates a follower, then the follower token may receive mcp:session.close_self only when the binding has a leaderSessionKey; closing another session requires mcp:session.close and cannot be inferred from sessionId knowledge.

Given a browser JWT is presented to the MCP endpoint or webhook endpoint as the only credential, then the request is rejected before tool or webhook dispatch and the audit reason identifies a credential-boundary violation without logging the JWT.

Given an Origin header is present, then it must match allowedOrigins; when Origin is absent, the request is accepted only if the non-browser request still passes loopback or whitelist transport policy and presents a valid MCP capability token, fixed MCP access key, webhook key, or one-time claim code restricted to the claim bootstrap flow. Browser JWTs and uncredentialed MCP initialization are rejected before dispatch.
Given whitelist bind mode is requested with an empty externalWhitelist, then the config is rejected rather than opening a broader listener or silently falling back to external access.

Given a webhook key is created or rotated, then the secret material is generated with a CSPRNG and at least 32 bytes of entropy, only keyHash and metadata are persisted, and the full key is returned only in the creation or rotation response.

Given a webhook key is created, then allowed target, default agent profile, allowed mode such as send-only or open-or-send, and mcp:webhook.invoke scope are stored with the key; a request that overrides those bindings beyond its grant is rejected before assignment side effects.

Given a policy denial occurs, then the response uses one of the stable contract codes UNBOUND_ACTOR, INVALID_SCOPE, TARGET_NOT_FOUND, AMBIGUOUS_TARGET, STALE_SESSION_ID, TARGET_NOT_LIVE, INPUT_REJECTED_REPLAY_PENDING, INPUT_REJECTED_ENTER_POLICY, SELF_CLOSE_DENIED_NO_LEADER, MCP_PORT_REBIND_FAILED, WEBHOOK_KEY_INVALID, or a documented successor code.

Given an authenticated UI administrator generates or regenerates the fixed MCP access key, then the server creates at least 32 bytes of CSPRNG secret material, serializes concurrent config writes, persists only its SHA-256 hash, invalidates the previous key immediately including already initialized MCP transport sessions, and returns the new plaintext key only in that generation response. A valid fixed key authenticates a non-session-bound MCP actor with exactly mcp:sessions.list, mcp:sessions.search, mcp:message.paste, and mcp:message.submit scopes; it grants no session creation, close, alias, status, or self identity privilege.

Given the server starts with persisted workspace tabs that do not yet have MCP registry bindings, when registry reconciliation runs, then each active tab receives a stable sessionKey binding without changing WorkspaceTab.name, nameSource, terminalTitle, recovery metadata, or the current runtime sessionId.

Given a persisted registry binding refers to a tab that no longer exists in workspace state, when reconciliation runs, then the bindingLifecycle becomes retired and the sessionKey is not reassigned to a different tab.

Given a persisted registry binding refers to a recoverable tab whose runtime session was recreated during orphan recovery, when reconciliation completes, then currentSessionId and generation match the recovered WorkspaceTab values before MCP list, search, or whoami can return the binding.

Given an active tab has no live SessionManager session and is not recovered, when reconciliation runs, then the binding is marked closed or retired according to tab recoverability and is excluded from default live session search.

Given reconciliation creates, updates, closes, or retires bindings, then the operation records counts and non-secret diagnostics in audit or startup logs so operators can distinguish backfilled, active, closed, and retired bindings.

Given registry reconciliation encounters malformed persisted registry data, then the invalid entries are rejected or quarantined without preventing workspace tabs from loading or assigning duplicate sessionKeys.

Given the UI admin is authenticated with the existing browser UI auth, then GET and PATCH /api/mcp-control/config expose and update enabled, bindMode, host, port, transportSecurity, trustedProxies, externalWhitelist, allowedOrigins, status, lastError, and lastRebindResult without accepting MCP runtime actor tokens as UI admin credentials.

Given the UI admin manages agent profiles, then GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE /api/mcp-control/agents use a schema containing id, displayName, command, args, aliases, isDefault, enabled, kickoffPrompt, mcpClientConfigMode, createdAt, and updatedAt.

Given an agent profile is saved through REST or UI, then the server rejects an empty command, command strings containing NUL or control characters, non-array args, duplicate aliases, invalid mcpClientConfigMode, multiple defaults, and kickoff prompts over the configured size limit.

Given webhook keys are managed, then POST /api/mcp-control/webhooks, POST /api/mcp-control/webhooks/:id/rotate, and DELETE /api/mcp-control/webhooks/:id return full key or full URL only on create or rotate responses and return only key id, masked key, bound target/profile/mode/scope, last used, expiry, revoked state, and rate-limit status in list responses.

Given live sessions are managed, then GET /api/mcp-control/sessions and PATCH /api/mcp-control/sessions/:sessionKey/alias return redacted live session data and update aliases through the same WorkspaceTab.name and nameSource user path as MCP set_alias.

Given the live sessions tab offers refresh, search test, reply test, alias edit, or close actions, then reply and close operations reuse MCP policy services, destructive close requires an explicit confirmation dialog, and close cannot bypass REL-MCP-001 lifecycle safety.

Given a REST validation or policy error occurs, then the response has a stable error shape with code, message, requestId or auditId, and field errors when applicable, and it does not include raw tokens, raw webhook keys, full query strings, or raw long prompts.

Given the frontend receives a one-time webhook URL after create or rotate, then it may display and copy that URL in the current response flow only; subsequent local state, persisted UI history, and list responses retain masked key material only.

Given the Tools dialog needs live-session search data, when it calls GET /api/mcp-control/sessions with an optional query parameter, then the server applies the same search semantics as buildergate.session.search, returns redacted session records keyed by stable sessionKey, and includes no raw MCP token, webhook key, or hidden terminal payload.

Given the Tools dialog runs a search diagnostic, when it calls POST /api/mcp-control/sessions/search-test with query text and optional filters, then the response returns matched sessionKey, alias, workspace, status, and match reason data or a stable validation error without mutating session state.

Given the Tools dialog runs a leader reply diagnostic, when it calls POST /api/mcp-control/sessions/:sessionKey/reply-test, then the request is routed through SessionInputGateway using the same policy as buildergate.message.reply_to_leader, returns accepted/rejected status with requestId or auditId, and never bypasses hidden, replay, or newline submit guards.

Given the Tools dialog closes a live session, when it calls POST /api/mcp-control/sessions/:sessionKey/close, then the request must include an explicit confirmation token or equivalent UI confirmation marker, must reuse REL-MCP-001 close lifecycle rules, and must return stable errors for stale, missing, already-closed, or unauthorized targets.

Given the UI lists webhook keys, when it calls GET /api/mcp-control/webhooks or mcpControlApi.listWebhooks(), then the response includes only keyId, maskedKey, bound target/profile/mode/scope, lastUsedAt, expiresAt, revoked state, and rate-limit status; full key material and full webhook URLs are never returned by list responses.

Given an agent command profile is created or updated, then displayName is required after trimming, must be between 1 and 80 Unicode scalar values, must reject NUL and control characters, and duplicate displayName values are allowed only because the stable id remains the unique profile key and UI responses include id plus command summary for disambiguation.

Given profile validation fails for displayName, command, args, aliases, mcpClientConfigMode, default selection, or kickoff prompt size, then the REST response uses the same stable error shape as IR-MCP-002 with field-specific errors and no secret material.

Given a webhook invocation presents a key only in the configured header, then the request is accepted if the key is valid and all whitelist, Origin, rate-limit, scope, target, and prompt policies pass; redaction and audit treatment are identical to query-key invocation.

Given a webhook invocation presents both query key and header key, then the request is accepted only when they identify the same non-revoked key and is rejected with WEBHOOK_KEY_INVALID or a documented successor when they conflict.

Given MCP or UI code updates agentStatus, then only unknown, starting, ready, busy, waiting_input, completed, and failed are accepted; invalid values are rejected, and accepted values are reflected consistently in buildergate.session.list, buildergate.session.search, buildergate.session.whoami, and GET /api/mcp-control/sessions responses.

Given a webhook key is created or rotated, then the full secret key and full webhook URL are returned only in that create or rotate response flow; list responses, persisted UI state, audit logs, local UI history, and subsequent config reads retain only keyId, maskedKey, hash, and non-secret metadata.

Given webhook header-key mode is enabled, then the default accepted header name is X-BuilderGate-Webhook-Key unless the admin config sets webhookKeyHeaderName to another non-empty token header name; query and header credentials share the same redaction, audit, hashing, scope, whitelist, Origin, and rate-limit pipeline.

Given webhook rate limiting is applied, then limits are evaluated per keyId and effective client IP with configurable windowSeconds and burstLimit fields; when omitted, safe defaults are used and exposed in redacted control status without weakening enforcement.

Given a webhook request exceeds rate limits, prompt size, transport policy, Origin policy, or key policy, then the denial uses stable codes WEBHOOK_RATE_LIMITED, WEBHOOK_PROMPT_TOO_LARGE, MCP_TRANSPORT_DENIED, MCP_ORIGIN_DENIED, WEBHOOK_KEY_INVALID, or a documented successor code and records a non-secret audit reason.

Given DELETE /api/mcp-control/webhooks/:id succeeds, then the key is revoked rather than hard-deleted, the response includes keyId, revoked true, revokedAt, and auditId, list responses show the revoked state without full key material, and a second delete returns an idempotent already-revoked success or a stable WEBHOOK_KEY_REVOKED code without reactivating the key.

Given buildergate.session.list omits includeSelf, then includeSelf defaults to true; when includeSelf is false, the caller's own bound session is excluded while other authorized live bindings remain visible according to scope and filter policy.

Given buildergate.session.search evaluates a query, then the searchable fields include user alias, tab name, agentKind, role, cwd, and recovery command metadata, with exact user alias matches still ranked ahead of weaker matches and ambiguous equal-rank matches rejected with explicit candidates.

Given a deferred buildergate.session.close_self job fails after the MCP response has flushed, then the follower session remains observable as failed or closing-failed, the failure is audited, and if the leader binding is still live and reply is permitted, a failure message is delivered to the leader through SessionInputGateway.

Given replay or screen-repair state is pending for a target session, then MCP or webhook input rejection uses the stable code INPUT_REJECTED_REPLAY_PENDING and does not substitute an implementation-defined equivalent code.

Given POST /api/mcp-control/sessions/:sessionKey/close is called, then the request must include confirmClose true, expectedSessionKey equal to the path sessionKey, and a current confirmationNonce issued by the UI; missing, stale, mismatched, or false confirmation data is rejected with CLOSE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED or a documented successor before any lifecycle side effect.

Given whitelist bind mode is configured with an empty externalWhitelist, then validation rejects the config with MCP_WHITELIST_EMPTY; given a non-loopback request does not match the configured whitelist, then request guarding rejects it with MCP_WHITELIST_DENIED or a documented successor code before MCP or webhook dispatch.

Given an audit or status payload includes promptPreview, then it is derived from prompt text only after secret redaction, control characters and CR/LF sequences are normalized to single spaces, leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed, and the preview is truncated to the configured promptPreviewMaxChars without storing or returning the full prompt.

Given MCP operational status is requested through the Tools dialog or control API, then it includes redacted recentAuditEvents limited by auditRecentEventsLimit, with auditId, timestamp, event category, stable code, redacted target/session reference, and no raw token, webhook key, full URL, or raw prompt material.

Given an admin configures webhookKeyHeaderName, then Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto, Host, and Content-Length are rejected as forbidden header names; accepted custom names must be non-empty token header names and are reflected in redacted config status.

Given webhook credentials are created or rotated, then any earlier create-only UI wording is interpreted as create-or-rotate one-time secret response; fullKey and fullUrl may appear only in that immediate response, and all subsequent UI, REST list, config, audit, or history surfaces remain masked.

Given MCP or REST responses expose agentStatus, then the only wire values are unknown, starting, ready, busy, waiting_input, completed, and failed; frontend API examples and runtime validation must reject and surface invalid values instead of preserving arbitrary strings.

Given MCP or REST responses expose bindingLifecycle, then the only wire values are live, closing, closed, retired, failed, and closing-failed; legacy or example values such as active must be normalized or rejected before list, search, whoami, and Tools dialog responses are produced.

Given FR-MCP-002 AC-2 permits an equivalent observable status for replay-pending rejection, IR-MCP-004 AC-9 and this requirement take precedence and require INPUT_REJECTED_REPLAY_PENDING unless a documented successor code explicitly supersedes it.

Given IR-MCP-003 AC-4 permits an equivalent UI confirmation marker for live-session close, IR-MCP-004 AC-10 and this requirement take precedence and require confirmClose true, expectedSessionKey matching the path sessionKey, and a current confirmationNonce before any close lifecycle side effect.

Given FR-MCP-005 AC-6 describes full webhook key display in the creation response, IR-MCP-004 AC-1 and this requirement take precedence and define the one-time response set as create or rotate only, while revoke, list, config, and history responses remain masked.

Given the server process environment carries `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, when a session is created, then that variable is absent from the environment the PTY is spawned with, and the same test asserts the variable really was set on the server process so the absence is not vacuous.

Given the server process environment carries the twelve variables a Claude Code session exports — `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, `CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH`, `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`, `CLAUDECODE`, `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` and `AI_AGENT` — when a session is created, then none of the twelve is present in the spawned environment. The five that carry no `CLAUDE_CODE_` prefix are named individually, because a rule written against that prefix alone passes the first seven and fails these.

Given a variable named `CLAUDE_ANYTHING_ADDED_LATER` that no version of the tool ships today, then it is removed as well: the rule is a prefix rule and not a list of known names, so a variable added to the namespace next year is covered without anyone editing it.

Given the server process environment carries `PATH`, `HOME`, `USERPROFILE` and other variables outside the rule, when a session is created, then every one of them is present in the spawned environment with its value unchanged, and the number of variables removed equals the number the process carried that the rule names. Without the count, a rule that removed everything would satisfy the absences above.

Given a bash session whose OSC 133 integration sets `BASH_ENV`, when that session is created, then `BASH_ENV` is present with the integration script path. This is judged as the presence of a variable the rule never names rather than as an ordering guard: no ordering of a rule over these names can remove `BASH_ENV`, and the ordering that is actually pinned — the rule before the `envPatch` merge — is AC-6's.

Given a session created with an `envPatch` naming `CLAUDE_CODE_FORCE_SESSION_PERSISTENCE`, then that variable is present in the spawned environment with the value the caller gave, even though the rule would otherwise take it; and the inherited variables are still gone, so the patch does not turn the rule off wholesale. This pins that the patch is merged over the filtered base rather than under it.

Given a variable whose name merely mentions the namespace without beginning with it, such as `MY_CLAUDE_SETTING` or `NOT_AI_AGENT`, and given `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, when a session is created, then all three are present in the spawned environment. The rule is a prefix rule plus one exact name, and a substring match would take variables that belong to the user rather than to the host.

Given an environment entry whose value is `undefined`, when it is filtered, then the key is absent from the result rather than carried with the literal string `undefined`. A spread would have carried it.

Given a window whose placement is `floating`, when 최대화 is pressed, then the placement becomes `stage` and `floating` is recorded as the previous placement; when 최대화 is pressed again, then the placement returns to `floating` and the window is drawn at the rect it held before.
Given a window whose placement is `stage` with no recorded previous placement, when 최대화 is pressed, then the placement becomes `floating`.
Given a window is open, then its title bar carries exactly four controls — 저장, 최대화, 최소화 and the dialog close button — and no 터미널 채움 control exists.

Given a window in `stage`, when the user drags or resizes it, then the placement becomes `floating` and the rect at the start of the interaction equals the rect the window had in its previous placement state.

Given `Rnd` reports a drag or resize whose resulting rect equals the rect the window already holds — which it does for every press of a title bar control, the title bar being the drag handle — then no rect reaches the host and the placement is unchanged.

Given the stage container measures to rect S, when a window is in `stage`, then its rect equals S; when S subsequently changes through a resize, then the window rect updates to the new S without any sidebar, header, or tab bar pixel constant appearing in the computation.

Given a `floating` window and a drag whose requested position would place part of the window over the sidebar, header, or tab bar, then the resulting rect is fully contained in the stage rect; and given a drag whose requested position is fully inside the stage rect, then the resulting rect differs from the pre-drag rect by exactly the requested delta.

Given no cached geometry exists, when a window opens on a desktop layout, then its size is `INITIAL_EDITOR_WINDOW_VIEWPORT_RATIO` of the viewport in each axis, except where that exceeds the stage, which bounds it, or falls below `EDITOR_WINDOW_MIN_SIZE`, which raises it; the test states the viewport it runs at and which of the three decided each axis and its position is centred inside the stage — the box the window is confined to — rather than inside the viewport, and never smaller than `EDITOR_WINDOW_MIN_SIZE`.
Given the mobile layout is rendered, when a window opens, then its placement is `stage`, the cached geometry is neither read nor written, and the window can be neither dragged nor resized.

Given a window whose editor body has been changed so that it differs from the content read from disk when the window opened, when the window is minimized and then restored, then the editor component instance is the same instance as before and the body still differs from the on-disk content in exactly the same way.
Given `minimized` is true, then the window surface carries `display: none` while the editor component remains mounted; no unmount and no remount is observed for that window.
Given a window in `stage`, when it is minimized and then restored, then its placement state is still `stage`; the same holds for a window in `floating`.

Given all three visibility terms hold, then the window is visible; and for each of the three terms individually, given that term alone is made false with the other two held true, then the window is hidden and still mounted.

Given a window whose terminal tab is switched away from, and given that tab is then deleted so its registry entry is gone, then the window is still visible and still holds the body typed into it; and while it is the active tab the window's 저장 control renders disabled, so the loss of the tab is reported rather than hidden. The condition is on the active tab because there is one save control per window and it acts on whichever document is in front.

Given workspace A holds an open document with unsaved text and the user switches to workspace B, then A's window carries `display: none` while its document panel stays mounted; and on returning to A the same editor instance is on screen with that text intact.

Given several documents are open in one window, then every one of their panels is mounted and all but the active tab's carry `display: none`; and text typed into a hidden panel is still there when its tab is selected.

Given a window bound to tab T, when T restarts and `tab.sessionId` is replaced, then `documentId` is unchanged and the `EditorView` instance is the same one as before the restart. The canonical statement of this obligation is FR-MDE-005; this criterion judges the hiding rule on top of it.

Given the user types into the editor, then the `markdownSource` prop value passed to the editor stays at the content read at open time while the editor's own body diverges from it, confirming the prop is not driven as a controlled value. The canonical statement of this obligation is FR-MDE-005; this criterion judges the hiding rule on top of it.

Given an editor window that is registered in the modeless stack but is not its last entry, when a `pointerdown` occurs on its title bar, then its token is the last entry of the modeless stack afterwards. The effect is read from the stack rather than from overlapping windows, because one window per workspace and one visible workspace leave no two editor windows on screen together.

Given the same window, when a `pointerdown` occurs on an element nested inside its editor content rather than on the window surface itself, then the window is still raised, showing the handler runs in the capture phase.

Given a `pointerdown` on an editor window, then the raise handler calls neither `stopPropagation` nor `preventDefault`: a listener attached to the pressed descendant still receives the event and the default caret placement or focus change still occurs.

Given a raise is performed, then the order of the window surfaces among their parent's child nodes is identical before and after the raise, and a text selection drag begun by that same `pointerdown` continues to extend as the pointer moves.

Given `raise` is called with the token of a window that is already front-most, then the modeless stack afterwards holds the same entries in the same order as before the call, that window is still its last entry, and subscribers are notified at most once. In the same test the call is shown to have reached the stack rather than being dropped: `raise` invoked with the token of the window immediately behind the front-most one moves that window to the end of the modeless stack and notifies subscribers, so a `raise` that is a no-op for every token fails this criterion.

Given a modal dialog is open and an editor window is present, when the editor window is raised, then the modal's `isTopmost` remains true and its Escape handling and Tab containment behave exactly as they do with no editor window present.

Given each of the six existing modal call sites is opened with no editor window present, then it is topmost in the modal stack, Escape closes it, and Tab cycles within it without reaching anything behind it. These are stated as the behaviour itself rather than as a comparison against the pre-split build: that build is not in the repository, so a criterion phrased as "unchanged from before" names a baseline nobody can open and cannot be failed by any implementation.

Given a window registered under `editorWindowDialogId(workspaceId)`, when `raiseDialogById` is called with that id and `'modeless'`, then it returns true and the window's token is the last entry of the modeless stack; and given an id no window is registered under, then it returns false and neither stack changes. This is the path that opening a file and choosing a tray entry both take to raise a window they do not own.

Given tab T with target rect (x, y, w, h) and n windows already docked to T holding the steps 0 through n-1 with no gap among them, where n is 0, 1, 2, or 3, when a further window enters `docked` on T, then its rect is exactly (x + 28n, y + 28n, w - 28n, h - 28n) and that rect is fully contained in (x, y, w, h). The no-gap condition is what makes the lowest free step equal n here; AC-7 covers the case where a gap exists, and without this condition the two criteria would demand different steps for the same arrangement.

Given one window already docked to tab T, when a second window is docked to T, then the two rects are not equal: they differ by exactly 28 in x and by exactly 28 in y, and the second is 28 smaller in both width and height.
Given four windows already docked to tab T, when a fifth is docked to T, then `k` wraps to 0 and the fifth window's rect equals the first window's rect exactly.

Given a target rect whose own width is at least 320 and whose own height is at least 240, but for which (w - 28k) is below 320 or (h - 28k) is below 240 for the step k that the count would assign, when the window enters `docked`, then it is placed with k = 0 and its rect equals the full target rect.

Given one minimized window docked to tab T and one window docked to T whose tab is not the active tab, when a new window enters `docked` on T, then it receives k = 2; and given instead one `floating` window and one `stage` window bound to T, then a new window entering `docked` receives k = 0.

Given window A is docked to T with k = 0, when A moves to `floating`, then B is docked to T and receives k = 0, and then A returns to `docked` through the 터미널 채움 control, then A's recomputed rect differs from B's rect.

Given three windows docked to T at steps 0, 1, and 2, when the window at step 1 is closed, then the rects of the remaining two windows are unchanged, and the next window to enter `docked` on T is placed at step 1.

Given a target terminal area whose own width is below 320 or whose own height is below 240, when a window enters `docked` on it, then k is 0 and the window's width and height equal the target area's own width and height. The box actually rendered for that window, measured rather than computed, is not widened to 320 and not heightened to 240, and is fully contained in the target area, so no part of it extends over a neighbouring tile.

Given the n-th editor window in the modeless stack, then the layer value computed for it equals 3000 + n * 20 while that value is at most 3980, and equals 3980 for every larger n; and the z-index actually applied to that window's `.window-dialog` surface equals the layer value plus one, so it is 3001 + n * 20, capped at 3981. Given two editor windows sitting at different stack indices below the cap, then their applied surface values differ from each other, showing each window received its own `layerIndex` rather than the fixed 0 that `dialogStack.ts:52-55` returns for a dialog that was never registered.

Given `createWindowDialogBehaviorModel` is called without a `mode` field, then it behaves as `mode = 'modal'` and produces layer z-index 5000 + layerIndex * 20; and `frontend/tests/unit/windowDialogContract.test.ts` passes unchanged, showing the set of returned fields did not grow.

Given any editor window and any of the modal surfaces, then the editor window's z-index is strictly less than 5000 for a `WindowDialog` modal, 5100 for `.command-preset-toast`, 9999 for `.modal-overlay`, and 10000 and 10001 for the context menu and its submenu.
Given any editor window, then its z-index is strictly greater than 2 for the terminal layer, 12 for the tile parts, 100 for the settings page and font-size toast, and 1000 for the mobile surfaces.
Given a `WindowDialog` modal is open and `.command-preset-toast` is showing, then the toast renders above the dialog, confirming the modal band was not raised.

Given one or more editor windows are open and a `WindowDialog` modal is then opened, then the modal renders above every editor window and the editor windows are `inert`: they cannot receive focus or pointer input until the modal closes.

Given a document bound to tab T with unsaved edits, when T restarts so that `tab.id` is unchanged and `tab.sessionId` is replaced, then the document is still open with the same editor instance and the same unsaved body, and the next save call carries the new session ID rather than the old one.

Given any persisted editor document record, then it contains the tab ID and contains no session ID field; and given a stored record produced before a tab restart, then restoring it after the restart still resolves a session ID through the tab.

Given the session of tab T is disconnected while T itself still exists, then the document bound to T stays open and a save attempt is issued; on failure the document stays dirty and shows the error in its own banner, and the window's placement state is untouched.

Given a window holding a document bound to tab T and a second document bound to a different tab, when T is closed while its document is the active tab, then the window's 저장 control and Ctrl+S are disabled and a 저장 불가 badge appears in the title bar; and when the second document's tab is then selected, the same 저장 control is enabled again and the badge is gone. The window's placement state and rect are the same values throughout. There is one save control per window and it acts on the active document, so the two documents' save states are observed one after the other rather than side by side — a criterion asserting both at once would describe a screen this window cannot produce.

Given a document with unsaved content whose tab has been closed, when the user closes that document, then the prompt shown is the 저장할 수 없습니다 branch and not the ordinary save prompt, and choosing to close discards the body without attempting a write.
Given persisted state containing two documents, one naming a tab that exists at restore time and one naming a tab that does not, then only the first is restored and the second is dropped.

Given a document bound to tab T, then its `documentId` equals the normalized absolute file path; and when T restarts, then `documentId` is unchanged and the `EditorView` instance is the same object as before the restart. The canonical statement of this obligation is FR-MDE-005; this criterion judges the tab binding on top of it.

Given the port is complete, then all of the following hold inside this repository, with no path in any other checkout read: `frontend/src/editor/vendor/atomic-editor/LICENSE` exists and its text contains the MIT permission notice; the entry barrel `frontend/src/editor/index.ts` exists and exports `doculightExtensions` together with the React editor component that `EditorWindow` mounts, and every symbol `EditorWindow` imports from `frontend/src/editor/` resolves through that barrel; and `frontend/src/editor/` contains exactly 25 `.ts` or `.tsx` files outside any `__tests__` directory plus exactly 2 CSS files, `styles/editor.css` and `vendor/atomic-editor/styles/inline-preview.css`, for 27 files in total, counted by a rule that excludes known non-source entries rather than by the same extension rule that produces the 25, so that a file the extension rule cannot see still moves this count; and those 27 files excluding the entry barrel total exactly 7,296 lines. The barrel is excluded from the line count because it is the one ported file this repository must extend: the symbols `EditorWindow` needs are not all re-exported by the barrel as copied, and the single-entry rule above requires adding those re-exports, so a fixed line count on the barrel would contradict the same criterion. Its ported form is 37 lines, and only re-exports may be added to it.

Given the editor is mounted with `documentId` D, then D is the document's absolute path and is not derived from the body, so a change to the body cannot by itself recreate the EditorView. This app produces neither half of that transition directly: the body is read once at open and no path changes `markdownSource` on a mounted editor, and the render site keys each document panel by `filePath`, so a different document is already a different React element before the editor's identity rule is consulted. The criterion is therefore judged on what the window hands the editor — the window passes `documentId`, and that value is the file path rather than anything derived from the body — and the E2E that covers it records that the remount transition itself has no path through this app rather than simulating one. A test that opened two files with identical content would not judge this: the render key already forces a remount there, so the editor's identity rule could be broken and that test would still pass.

Given the editor is mounted and the user types text T, then the host's change callback is invoked with a value containing T, and the `markdownSource` prop value passed on the next render is still the value given at mount.

Given the host renders twice with unchanged inputs, then the `extensions` array passed on the second render is reference-identical (`===`) to the one passed on the first; and toggling `readOnly` changes the editor's read-only state while the EditorView instance stays the same object.

Given a window bound to tab T is editing file F, when T is restarted so that its `sessionId` is replaced, then the `documentId` passed to the editor is unchanged and equals the normalized absolute path of F, and the EditorView instance is the same object as before the restart.

Given the ported dependencies, then `frontend/package.json` declares `mermaid` at `^11.4.1` and declares `katex` and `shiki` and at least one `@codemirror/*` and one `@lezer/*` package, and `tsc` over the frontend exits zero with the ported tree included in the program.

Given the ported tree, then a recursive search of `frontend/src/editor/` for `fetch(`, `/api/`, `localStorage` and `react-router` returns zero matches, and the same search run for the five `doculightExtensions` callback names (`onTagClick`, `onAttach`, `suggestWikiLinks`, `onOpenWikiLink`, `resolveWikiLink`) returns a nonzero number of matches.

Given a session whose cwd is C, when a write is requested for a relative path inside C with content S, then the response is a success, the file's bytes decode from UTF-8 to exactly S, and the first three bytes are not the UTF-8 BOM.

Given content whose text mixes CRLF and LF line endings, when it is written and read back as bytes, then the bytes are identical to the bytes of the submitted content, with no line ending added, removed or converted.

Given a path that escapes the session cwd (for example a parent-directory traversal, or an absolute path outside C), when a write is requested, then the response is an error, no file is created at the escaped location, and a control write to a legal path inside C in the same test succeeds.

Given a path whose extension is in the blocked extension list, when a write is requested, then the response is an error and no file is created; and in the same test the identical content written to a `.md` path inside C succeeds.

Given a path that resolves inside a configured blocked path, when a write is requested, then the response is an error and no file is created; and in the same test a control write of the identical content to a legal path inside C that is outside every blocked path succeeds, so a route that rejected every write could not satisfy this criterion.

Given a path inside C at which no file exists, when a write is requested, then the file is created with the submitted content; and given an existing file whose content is longer than the submitted content, when a write is requested, then the file's resulting length equals the length of the submitted content.

Given `fileApi.writeFile(sessionId, path, content)`, when it is called, then exactly one request is issued, to `/api/sessions/<sessionId>/files/write`, with method POST and a body carrying `path` and `content`; and the function's first parameter is `sessionId`, matching the other seven `fileApi` functions.
Given the server answers a write with an error status, when `fileApi.writeFile` is called, then the returned promise rejects rather than resolving, so the caller can keep the document dirty.

Given a write requested under a session ID for which no session exists, then the response is an error, no file is created anywhere, and the rejection is produced by the session existence check that runs ahead of any path resolution, mirroring `FileService.ts:225`; and in the same test an otherwise identical write to a legal path under a session that does exist succeeds, so the criterion is not satisfied by a route that rejects everything.

Given the file size limit the write path enforces on decoded content, when it is compared with the `maxFileSize` the read path applies, then both read the same configuration field rather than two values kept in step, so no file the read path serves is rejected by the write path for its size — including content whose JSON encoding expands it, because the transport bound carrying the request is a separate and larger value derived from that same field, sized so that the worst expansion the read path actually admits still fits; and given content larger than the file size limit, when a write is requested, then the response reports it as too large (413) rather than an unhandled server error (500) and no file is written; and in the same test content of exactly that limit is written successfully with its stored bytes matching the submitted content, so a route that rejected every oversized body could not satisfy this criterion; and the limit is read when the request arrives, so raising `maxFileSize` at runtime makes the larger file writable without a restart.

Given a window whose document has just been read from disk, then its title carries no `*`; when the user types into the editor, then the title carries a trailing `*` and the body ref holds the typed text.

Given the editor window of the current workspace holds DOM focus and the window of another workspace is dirty and frontmost in the modeless stack, when `Ctrl+S` is pressed, then exactly one write is issued and its path is A's file; no write is issued for B's file.

Given DOM focus is outside every editor window, when `Ctrl+S` is pressed, then no write is issued; and in the same test, when focus is then moved inside a window and `Ctrl+S` is pressed again, then exactly one write is issued.
Given DOM focus is inside an editor window, when `Ctrl+S` is pressed, then `preventDefault()` is called on that keyboard event.

Given a dirty window, when the title bar save button is pressed, then the same save function is invoked with the same arguments as a focus-scoped `Ctrl+S` would produce, and on a successful response the `*` is removed from the title.
Given a dirty window whose write fails, then the title still carries `*`, an error banner is rendered inside that window, and no `MessageBox` is opened.
Given a window bound to tab T saved once, when T is restarted so that its `sessionId` changes from S1 to S2 and the window is saved again, then the second write is issued with S2.

Given a dirty window whose tab is alive, when the close button is pressed, then a three-choice confirmation appears; choosing save with a failing write leaves the window open with the error banner shown; choosing don't save closes the window; choosing cancel leaves the window open and still dirty.

Given a dirty window whose bound tab has closed, when the close button is pressed, then the prompt shown is the cannot-save prompt and not the three-choice save prompt; and in that state the save button is disabled and `Ctrl+S` issues no write. The canonical statement of the tab-closed behaviour, including this separate prompt and the disabled save path, is CON-MDE-002; this criterion judges the save flow on top of it.
Given a window that is not dirty, when the close button is pressed, then it closes immediately with no prompt rendered.

Given tab mode with a session whose path bar shows cwd C, when the path is right-clicked, then a context menu opens containing exactly the items `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md` and `AGENTS.md`; and in the same test a plain left click on that path still invokes the copy handler.
Given grid mode with a tile whose path bar shows cwd C, when the path is right-clicked, then the same three items open, so both render sites of `MetadataRow` carry the handler.

Given a chosen item whose file exists, then a read is issued with the bound tab's current `sessionId` and the path resolved against C, and a document bound to that tab's `tabId` is added to the current workspace's editor window and becomes its active tab.

Given a chosen item whose read returns 404, then a confirmation is shown; when it is confirmed, then a write of empty content is issued for that path and a document then opens; when it is cancelled, then no write is issued and no document opens.
Given a chosen item whose read fails with an error other than 404, then a `MessageBox` is shown and no document opens.

Given exactly one document is already open on the resolved absolute path P, when the same item is chosen again, then the number of open documents is still exactly one, that document becomes the active tab of its window, the window is raised to the front of the modeless stack, and no read and no write is issued for P.

Given two tabs whose `cwd` values are identical and a document opened on `CLAUDE.md` from the first tab, when `CLAUDE.md` is chosen from the second tab, then exactly one document exists for that path and it is still bound to the first tab's `tabId`. The same holds when the two tabs belong to different workspaces: the second choice moves the user to the workspace holding the document rather than opening a second one, because the key is compared across workspaces.

Given this work is complete, then the three items are produced by a module other than `frontend/src/utils/contextMenuBuilder.ts`, that file is unchanged, and the existing context menu tests covering FR-ARCH-001 and FR-ARCH-004 through FR-ARCH-006 pass unchanged.
Given no editor document is open in any workspace, then the tray icon is not rendered; and in the same test, when a document is opened, then the icon is rendered.

Given editor documents exist only in a workspace other than the current one, then the tray icon is still rendered, and its badge shows the total count across every workspace rather than the count of the current one.

Given the view mode toggle is rendered, then the tray icon is its immediately preceding sibling inside `header-right`. The toggle is hidden by two conditions (`Header.tsx:160` gates on `onToggleViewMode && !isMobile`), and on a desktop viewport neither leaves a reachable state for the second half of this rule: `App.tsx` passes `onToggleViewMode` only when a workspace is active, and with no active workspace the editor layer is not rendered either, so there is no tray icon to place. Given a mobile viewport, where the toggle is hidden while editor documents can still exist, then the tray icon is the first child of `header-right`. That half is judged on a mobile project rather than on Desktop Chrome, and a run that skips it reports the skip rather than counting it as covered.

Given workspace A holds documents D1 (dirty) and D2 (clean) and workspace B holds D3, when the tray icon is pressed, then the menu lists exactly D1, D2 and D3; the D1 entry carries `*` and the D2 entry does not; and each entry reads `워크스페이스 / 탭 | 경로` with the names of the workspace and the tab the document was opened from.

Given a minimized document open in workspace B while workspace A is current, when its tray entry is chosen, then the active workspace becomes B, `minimized` becomes false, that document's tab becomes the active tab of B's window, and the window is frontmost in the modeless stack.
Given the settings screen is showing and a tray entry is chosen, then the screen returns to the workspace screen and that document becomes visible.

Given a document whose path exceeds 56 characters, then its entry shows the path truncated from the left with the file name intact; and given a document whose workspace name or tab name is missing, then the entry renders `(이름 없음)` or `(닫힌 탭)` in that position rather than leaving it empty.
Given two visible documents and a third that is minimized, when the third's tray entry is chosen, then the other two remain visible and neither becomes minimized.

Given the tray entries have been built once, when the component re-renders with workspace and tab arrays that are new objects carrying the same names, then the entry list is not rebuilt; the guard is a source-text contract test asserting that the memo depends on a key derived from the names rather than on the arrays.

Given a workspace whose window holds two open documents whose editors contain the unsaved text U1 and U2, when the state is serialized, then the value written under `window_state_<workspaceId>` contains exactly two records, each carrying a tab ID and a file path, and neither U1 nor U2 appears anywhere in the serialized value.

Given the same serialized value, then each record carries exactly the two fields above and nothing else, and the value contains no session ID, no placement, no `minimized` flag and no coordinate under any name at any depth. The window the value was produced from is shown to have been floating, minimized and carrying a dragged rect, so every absence is one the input could have produced; a projection that spread its input fails this criterion.

Given a stored value naming documents for tabs T1 and T2 where only T1 exists in the workspace, when the reopen runs, then a document is reopened for T1 and none for T2, and T1's document is the active tab.

Given a stored value whose records are in the order D1, D2, D3, when the reopen runs, then the window's tabs appear in that same order; nothing re-sorts them by file path, by tab ID or by any other key.

Given a window the user drags to a new rect, then that rect is written under `buildergate.editor-window.geometry`; and no value is written to `buildergate.dialog.<id>.geometry` at any point, including when the window is closed.

Given a stored geometry whose size is below `EDITOR_WINDOW_MIN_SIZE` or whose origin lies outside the viewport, when it is read back, then the returned rect is at least `EDITOR_WINDOW_MIN_SIZE` in both dimensions and its origin is pushed back inside the viewport rather than its size being shrunk. The same input passed through `clampDialogRect` is shown to return a smaller-than-minimum size, so the two clamping rules are demonstrated to differ rather than asserted to.

Given a window moved to a rect R in workspace A, when the user switches to workspace B and opens a document there, then B's window renders at R; the remembered position and size are shared by every workspace because they live under one global key.

Given a window with unsaved text, when the workspace is switched away and back, then the editor instance is the same object, the unsaved text is still present, and no read of `window_state_<workspaceId>` occurred during the round trip.

Given no stored value under `window_state_<workspaceId>` or under the geometry key, or a stored value that fails to parse, or a storage that throws on read and on write, when the reopen runs, then no document is reopened, the window still opens at its default rect when a document is opened by hand, and no error is surfaced to the user.

Given a stored record whose file the read path can no longer open - deleted or moved between sessions - when the reopen runs, then that record produces no tab while every other record still reopens, and no error is surfaced to the user. This is not the case AC-9 covers: there the stored value itself is unreadable, so nothing can be reopened; here the value is well-formed and the failure is in the world it points at, so rejecting the whole batch would discard documents whose files are still present. The test asserts the surviving tab count directly rather than only the absence of an error, because an implementation that reopened nothing at all would also surface no error.

Given a window the user dragged to a rect R, when the page is reloaded, then the reopened window renders at R, read from the rendered box rather than from the store; and given the window was minimized before the reload, then the reopened one is not minimized. The placement state is not stored while the position is, so the two halves of this criterion must be judged together: a reopen that rebuilt the window from its defaults alone would satisfy the second half and fail the first.

Given a value written by the schema that stored `placement`, `placementBeforeStage`, `minimized` and `floatingRect`, when the reopen runs, then every record whose tab still exists is reopened and the four extra fields are ignored; and a record naming a missing tab is still dropped, so the tab filter is not skipped for an older value.
Given a tab set holding paths P1 and P2 with P1 active, when a tab for P2 is added, then the set still holds exactly two tabs in the same order and P2 becomes the active path.
Given a tab set holding P1, when a tab for P3 is added, then the set holds P1 and P3 in that order and P3 is the active path; a newly opened document is the one the user is looking at.

Given a tab set holding P1, P2 and P3 with P2 active, when P1 is closed, then the remaining tabs are P2 and P3 in that order and P2 is still the active path. The closed tab precedes the active one, so an implementation that tracked the active tab by index would move the activity to P3 here and fail.

Given a tab set holding P1, P2 and P3 with P2 active, when P2 is closed, then the active path becomes P3; and given instead that P3 was active when it was closed, then the active path becomes P2. Closing the active tab never leaves the set with tabs remaining and no active path.

Given a tab set holding one tab, when that tab is closed, then the set holds no tabs and the active path is null; and given a selection of a path the set does not hold, then the set is returned unchanged and no tab is created.

Given a window holding three open documents, then all three panels are mounted and the two inactive ones carry `display: none`; and text typed into one of them before switching away is still present when its tab is selected again.

Given a document with unsaved changes that is not the active tab, then its entry in the tab row carries a trailing `*` while the active tab's own entry carries none. Saving is deliberately not part of this criterion: the only save controls are the window's 저장 button and `Ctrl+S`, both of which act on the active document, so there is no user action that saves a document behind another tab and no state in which the marker could clear without the tab being selected first.
